plain_language_definition: The value the model tries to predict
why_it_matters: The target defines the question the model can answer

plain_language_definition: A variable used as an input to the model
why_it_matters: Features must be measured and available before prediction

plain_language_definition: One sample, observation, or record in the modeling table
why_it_matters: Rows define the evidence unit for modeling

plain_language_definition: Rows used to fit the model
why_it_matters: The model learns patterns from these rows
This estimates how the model works on data it did not fit

plain_language_definition: A simple model used for comparison
why_it_matters: Complex models must beat a simple standard to be useful

plain_language_definition: A model for predicting a number
why_it_matters: Used for salinity or dissolved oxygen style targets

plain_language_definition: A model for predicting a category
why_it_matters: Used for high versus lower salinity style targets

plain_language_definition: Information in features that unfairly reveals the target
why_it_matters: Leakage makes models look better than they are

plain_language_definition: Root mean squared error in the target unit
Mean absolute error in the target unit
why_it_matters: Easy to explain as average error size

plain_language_definition: Counts of correct and incorrect class predictions
why_it_matters: Shows false positives and false negatives
Useful when missing high-risk samples is costly
Useful when false alarms are costly

plain_language_definition: A short record of data features split metrics and limits
why_it_matters: Prevents black-box or undocumented model claims
Helps diagnose where regression models miss

plain_language_definition: How many rows are in each class
why_it_matters: A high accuracy can be misleading when one class dominates
